summary: We often watch rockets launch into space and wonder what they will discover, but have you ever wondered how much planning and decision-making happens before a mission even begins? That is why we developed Mission Frontier, an interactive Space Mission Design Game that lets people experience the challenges of planning a space mission themselves. Instead of simply watching a rocket launch, players become mission designers. They choose a mission objective, build their spacecraft, select scientific instruments such as cameras, radars and spectrometers, choose launch vehicles and orbits, and manage resources like fuel, mass, power, batteries, communication, data and budget. Our game addresses the Space Mission Design challenge by turning complex engineering concepts into an interactive experience where players learn by making decisions and seeing their results. Every choice matters. Adding an instrument may improve scientific observations, but it can also increase mass, power consumption and data requirements. Choosing the wrong combination of components or exceeding resource limits can affect the mission's success. We created Mission Frontier to help people understand the thinking behind space exploration and appreciate the work of engineers. Our goal is to make space mission planning easier to understand, exciting to explore and meaningful to learn.
details:
Mission Frontier is an interactive Space Mission Design Game that gives players an opportunity to experience the planning and challenges behind a space mission. Players begin by selecting a mission objective and then design their spacecraft by choosing essential systems such as power supply, batteries, communication systems, onboard computers and attitude control. They can also select scientific instruments such as cameras, spectrometers, radar and other payloads according to their mission goals. Next, players select a launch vehicle and target orbit before checking important mission resources, including spacecraft mass, power consumption, data capacity, communication limits and budget. Once the design is complete, they can run a mission simulation, observe the journey and evaluate their mission performance.

The main benefit is educational: instead of simply watching rockets travel into space, users learn why careful engineering decisions are necessary. Every component has a purpose, and adding or removing equipment can affect the mission's overall performance and success.

We developed the project using web development technologies, including React and Vite, with JavaScript, HTML and CSS, and used GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT to assist development. Our creative approach combines interactive game mechanics, spacecraft design, resource management and visual simulation. We considered scientific relevance, usability, educational value and the relationships between engineering decisions and mission outcomes.
